findings.what: Two direct `process.kill(-pgid, "SIGKILL")` in try/catch remain next to the new shared `signalGroup` (cleanup.js:52), which does the same thing synchronously. The group-kill mechanism is again written more than once in the same file (AP-014 residue of R-F4).
findings.fix: Call signalGroup(pgid, "SIGKILL") in both places. Behaviour is the same.

findings.what: Since R-F1 the whole E2eError message goes to stderr as is. Three messages carry text of the operator, not of a page: SELECTION_UNKNOWN (the argument of the command line), and CHROME_NOT_FOUND with the value of SAI_CHROME. They are not passed through safeText, so a newline or a line start `::` in an argument or in the variable can forge a log line. The source is the person who runs the command, so this is not an attack path; the safeText rule of S-F2 covers page and browser text only. Same kind as I4(2) of SECURITY-REVIEWER and I4 of the fixer.
findings.fix: Wrap `name` and `value` in safeText in those three messages (one line each), or leave as recorded; either way TEST-DESIGNER need not test it.

findings.what: The registry variable SAI_E2E_REGISTRY is read from the `env` option of launchBrowser, not from the process environment. A spec that calls launchBrowser or withBrowser with its own `env` object that lacks the variable (for example `{ SAI_CHROME: ... }`) is not recorded, so the safety net of S-F1 does not cover it. The normal call (no env option, or env spread from process.env) is covered, as probed. The next requirements (REQ-105..107) may pass a custom env.
findings.fix: Read the variable from process.env in noteBrowserForRunner (the spec process always has it), and keep `env` only for the child. Or document in tools/README.md that a custom env must carry the variable.

findings.what: The same two small helpers (first line of a text; cut to a length) are written in three modules (firstLine in page.js and console.js, oneLine in runner.js, cut in page.js and console.js). Not new in the fixes and not a finding of the first pass; recorded because the shared safeText now exists in errors.js and these could live next to it.
findings.fix: Optional: export firstLine from errors.js and import it; leave cut where it is.
